_comment: Maps each Drive subfolder name to a report type and the parser module that handles it. Add entries as new report parsers are built. Subfolders without a parser are ignored (logged) until one is added. Rent Roll and Residential AR Analytics now have parsers (parse_rent_roll, parse_delinquency); both expose parse(path) and tie out against the report's own total rows. Weekly Leasing Reports is still pending and trade-out data is hand-entered in the workbook's Lease Detail tab.

subfolders._comment: The EliseAI weekly funnel parses from here too, so it works wherever the gmail filing lands it. The pending entry below is for this folder's intended content -- the RealPage rate tracker -- which has never yet arrived. The glob is anchored with a leading * because the Gmail-to-Drive filing prefixes the arrival date: '2026-08-25 leasing_funnel_report_2026-08-25.xlsx'. fnmatch matches the whole name, so a pattern starting at 'leasing_' silently skipped every prefixed file.

Same report type as Residential AR Analytics -- the PM files delinquency summaries in both. A file present in both folders parses twice and the second store overwrites the first with identical content, which is harmless.
Leading * for the same reason as the Weekly Leasing Reports entry: filed copies carry a 'YYYY-MM-DD ' prefix.
The building-metrics CSV. No parse/accumulate step -- update.yml runs populate_building_metrics.py on the newest one after the scorecard fill, passing Drive's landed_at as the arrival time.

The Yardi Unit Directory: every unit's floorplan, square footage, bedrooms and baths, for all properties in one export. Routed by the property-code rows inside it and tied out against each section's own Total row.
